## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `priority:p3` · `domain:ui` · `area:records` · `pm:queue`. Option 1: the `simple` arm draws a self-contained inline entry, as every other arm does

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-04T13:55Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

**Why option 1, not "document the intersection".**
- One section contract across form types. objectstack-ai/objectstack#21704 fork 3 (ruled B) admits the inline arm on the page block without naming a form type. Five of six arms draw it. A `simple`-only exception would be a second contract that objectstack's section shape would have to carry.
- objectui#9884's pool intersection catches a **name-only** entry the object does not declare (a typo, or a stale name). An inline entry that carries its own `type` declares itself, so skipping it guards nothing.

**Direction:**
- `buildSectionFields`'s pooled branch (`sectionFields.ts` about `:480`–`:484`) draws an entry that carries its own `type`, the same way the pool-less branch does.
- Name-only entries keep the intersection and its warning.
- `ObjectFormSection.fields`' type (`packages/types/src/objectql.ts` about `:1497`) gains the form view's `{ field }` arm, which `sectionFields.ts` already draws.
- objectui's inline-sections test (`submitTargetRefusal.test.tsx`) adds the `simple` arm, so all six are run.

**Why p3.** The inline arm's measured writers (#21704's census: 7) are all in `plugin-form`'s README wizard and its tests, on the wizard arm, not on `simple`. Nothing drawn today goes missing. It closes a divergence before a writer reaches it.

**Routing:** `plugin-form`, so `domain:ui`. The type line rides the same PR.

**Serial:** objectui#11610 (`packages/types` form keys) and objectui#8347 (in flight on `packages/types/src/**`). The claim reads their file lists.
